summary: Forest-department campsite on the Ambika river in the hills near Vyara — riverside cottages and trails that pair with the Waghai belt.
description:
Padam Dungari sits just over the district line in Tapi, but travellers treat it as part of the same forest country as Waghai: an eco-campsite where the Ambika river comes off the Dang hills through a wooded valley, with cottages, tents, a riverside stretch made for slow mornings, and trails into the surrounding forest. It is among south Gujarat's better-known forest stays, popular with Surat weekenders.

The formula matches its Dang siblings — forest-department simplicity, mess meals when booked, guided walks on request — with somewhat easier access from the plains. Monsoon brings the river up and the crowds in; winter is calm and better for birds. Book ahead through the department's eco-tourism channels for any weekend.
highlights: Easier plains access than the interior campsites
Pairs with Waghai's garden, Gira Falls and Vansda NP

modes.road: Via Vyara from NH-53 or via the Waghai side; signed approach to the campsite

access.road_condition: Good, with a rural final stretch

timings.note: Day-visit window indicative; guests per booking

fees.note: Indicative day-visit fee; cottage tariffs separate

booking.notes: Stays via the forest department's eco-tourism portal; weekends fill early

seasonality.notes: Monsoon river season vs. calm birding winters — both work.

experience.photography_notes: River bends at dawn; the wooded valley holds mist into mid-morning in winter.

amenities.food: Campsite mess when booked; Vyara for the rest

warnings: River bathing only in marked gentle stretches — monsoon flow is strong
Weekend crowds bring litter; carry yours back

tips: Combine with a Waghai-belt day — garden, Gira Falls, Kilad
Book cottages over tents in monsoon; the river air soaks everything
